rows.currentScript: On the card you see swift. It points to very great speed. Fast matches that meaning quite closely. Slow is the opposite here; cheetah and race come from racing.
rows.whyRewrite: False claim: "cheetah and race come from racing". A cheetah is an animal, not something that comes from racing.

rows.currentScript: Look first at the word damp. It means a little bit wet. Moist says just the same thing. Dry means the reverse; towel and puddle are simply wet things.
rows.whyRewrite: False claim: "towel and puddle are simply wet things". A towel is a thing for drying, not a wet thing; "simply" is also the banned word's family.

rows.currentScript: Read the card word hollow. It means bare and quite unfilled. Empty points to that meaning. Solid works the opposite way; log and drum are hollow things.
rows.whyRewrite: Untrue claims: "It means bare and quite unfilled" (hollow does not mean bare) and "log and drum are hollow things" (a log is normally solid).

rows.currentScript: Your card holds the word rare. This word means fairly uncommon. Scarce means the same thing. Common means the reverse; coin and stamp are things people collect.
rows.whyRewrite: Wrong strength: "This word means fairly uncommon." Rare means not found often, not fairly uncommon; in a family whose distractors test strength, the gloss teaches the wrong one.

rows.currentScript: The card in front shows obedient. It describes doing just as told. Dutiful carries that meaning too. Disobedient means the reverse; dog and command belong to obeying.
rows.whyRewrite: Names a word not on the screen: "Dutiful carries that meaning too." The options are well-behaved, disobedient, dog and command; the key well-behaved is never named.

rows.currentScript: The word on the card is luminous. It describes strong and pouring light. Bright lands closest to it. Dull works the opposite way; moon and lamp give off light.
rows.whyRewrite: Untrue and unclear gloss: "It describes strong and pouring light." Luminous means giving off light, often a soft glow; "pouring light" is not a phrase a child can use.

rows.currentScript: The card shows the word notorious. It stands for widely bad fame. Infamous carries that same dark meaning. Reputable turns it around; criminal and headline belong to crime news.
rows.whyRewrite: Not readable English for a 9-11-year-old: "It stands for widely bad fame." The gloss does not parse, so the step to infamous is not shown.
Rapid as very fast; quick matches; slow opposite, race a thing, hurried correctly distinguished.
Timid as easily scared; shy matches; terrified too strong; quiet one part, polite different. True.
Sturdy as strong and well made; strong matches; unbreakable too far; heavy and wooden different. True.
Feeble as weak; frail matches; helpless too far; pale and elderly go with feeble. True.
Amiable as friendly and pleasant; friendly matches; grumpy opposite; cheerful and chatty correctly placed.
Exquisite as very beautiful; beautiful matches; pretty too weak, costly different; sharp is the exquisite-pain sense. True.
Benevolent as kind and wanting to do good; kind matches; saintly too far; polite and wealthy different. True.
Jovial as cheerful and friendly; cheerful matches; ecstatic too strong; silly and loud correctly placed.
Melancholy as sad and thoughtful; sad matches; heartbroken too strong; a gentle or slow tune is not always sad. True.
